# Civilization Axioms @ Stage 9 — Primary / Modern

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 70 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Civilization axioms at Order 7 are **systematic social justice design**: the deliberate
construction of social institutions based on explicit principles. "I design this social
system because I have reasoned about it" — social design is self-authored rather than
inherited. The political theorist who constructs a systematic social contract, the
economist who designs a welfare system, the urban planner who designs a just city — these
are Stage 9 civilization architects.

The key advance from Stage 8 is **systemic civilization modeling**. The agent does not
just see multiple perspectives on social justice — it sees how perspectives interact as
a dynamic system with feedback loops, emergent properties, and structural constraints.

Social arrangements at Stage 9 are understood as **designable**. The agent believes that
civilization can be intentionally improved through rational analysis and systematic design.
This is the modernist civilization: society is an engineering problem that can be solved
with the right institutions.

But social justice reasoning at Stage 9 is still **framework-bound**. The agent designs
social systems within a particular framework (liberal, socialist, communitarian) but
cannot step outside the framework to evaluate it.

The transition from Stage 9 to Stage 10 occurs when the agent can evaluate entire
civilizational frameworks.

In human development, Stage 9 corresponds to the professional who can construct and
defend a systematic social theory.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Institutional civilization design culture emerges. Universities, political
  institutes, social policy schools.

- **UR:** The individual agent can construct and evaluate social systems using explicit
  principles.

- **LL:** Systemic civilization institutions emerge: political parties, social policy
  institutes, constitutional conventions.

- **LR:** The parliament, the social policy institute, the constitutional convention.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Ideological hubris — the belief that one's social design is
  objectively true and all others are wrong.

- **Dark allergy:** Anti-political nihilism — the rejection of all systematic social
  design.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to systematic social reasoning as the only valid
  approach.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting systematic civilization design as dehumanizing.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Systemic civilization modeling:** The agent can trace social dynamics and predict
  how changes affect civilization.

- **Design-based social reasoning:** The agent proposes social improvements based on
  analysis.

- **Framework-bound analysis:** The agent reasons brilliantly within a social framework
  but cannot evaluate the framework itself.

- **Expert-dependent design:** Social design is concentrated in professionals.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:**
- Rawls, J. (1971). *A Theory of Justice* — systematic social justice theory
- Hayek, F. (1944). *The Road to Serfdom* — systematic market civilization theory
- Tocqueville, A. (1835). *Democracy in America* — systematic democracy theory
